status: File-service migration active; open, native/token byte IO, seek origins and record-stream spans complete and verified.

open.options: Scoped byte-width access and sharing enums; named create/truncate/exclusive/native booleans replace positional integers. The file service still owns path validation, native/stream selection, sharing and resource admission.
open.result: Transient result holds a signed 16-bit token (or -1) and missing flag. The registry owns every accepted token; errno remains the failure detail. Returned structs never enter saved records.
open.mode_boundary: MdOpenFlags retains its explicit unsigned 16-bit ABI/layout. StreamOpen decodes access, sharing, create/truncate and no-error policy once at the game/platform boundary. Retry timing, missing/nonmissing admission, error publication and handle assignment remain unchanged. Unrecognized sharing-bit combinations preserve their prior deny-none behavior.
open.effects: OutputFileString retains its existence check and create/truncate/append order. StarsCopyFile retains exclusive create and cleanup. The SDL OpenFile adapter still opens without truncation, validates identity/sharing, then truncates. Lower stream-mode parsing, exclusive creation, native identity and session token reuse/destruction retain their behavior.
open.tests: Before migration the actual token API passed read-only access, update without truncation, create with truncation, and OutputFileString append/new-file checks. The same assertions use named options/results afterward. Existing Unicode/missing/malformed-path, exception, session cleanup and file-service contract checks remain; invalid typed access still rejects before mutation.
open.initial_build_correction: The full build found one SDK OpenFile adapter call omitted from the first src/tests inventory. Its actual named request preserves check-before-truncate order; the inventory now includes compat/win32/src. An initial Windows build command also used the wrong contract target; corrected to stars-test-fileio.
open.test_harness: The actual Windows host build exposed an existing test-only cleanup branch requiring unavailable SDK declarations. Native path-test cleanup now uses std::filesystem with char8_t input and an error_code on every platform, retaining the removal assertion without SDL or SDK conversion scaffolding.

byte_and_seek.result_contract: A present count, including zero, reports transferred bytes; nullopt reports a failed operation through errno. Positive partial counts and persistent stream error/EOF state remain separately observable. No all-or-nothing write promise is added.
byte_and_seek.capacities: Real fixed arrays and their tails become byte spans; the SDK preserves null-pointer checks before forming views. Record-stream and raw element APIs still bridge their existing caller-supplied ranges pending physical-span migration.
byte_and_seek.provider: The actual COMPATFILEREADSCOPE provider and held-lock exception witness receive/return the same span/optional-count types. No old raw-pointer provider adapter remains. SDK _lread/_lwrite map optional results back to their unchanged native counts/LastError/EINTR contract.
byte_and_seek.seek_contract: Scoped NATIVESEEKORIGIN is carried through core, host, ZIP/library, metadata, SDK and test consumers. Integers exist only at the actual OS/SDK boundary; SDK invalid origins are rejected before conversion. The token helper retains its existing fallback-to-end behavior for a forced nonstandard origin. Existing 32/64-bit position and overflow rules remain.
byte_and_seek.layout: fileio.h gives transient standard-library/service values native packing and restores caller packing. The actual packed Win32 include fixture checks optional-count and native metadata alignment and packing restoration. No saved record uses these values.
byte_and_seek.reference_checks: Before migration the actual native/token functions passed byte/count/sentinel checks, explicit EOF observation, size queries preserving EOF, current/end/begin seeks, invalid native origins and POSIX empty-write effects. After migration the same checks use spans/results; the zero-write test also covers both native and buffered backends.
byte_and_seek.initial_test_corrections: A first reference assertion incorrectly expected every short native-descriptor read to set EOF; corrected it to perform a further read that returns zero at EOF, retaining prefix/sentinel checks. A Windows test initially used a buffered stream while expecting native truncation; expanded it to require native truncation and buffered ENOTSUP, preserving existing implementation behavior. A missed SDK pointer span extent was corrected before final compilation.
byte_and_seek.call_inventory_scope: 98 listed direct expressions across ten native/token byte/seek functions, plus the actual SDK read-provider invocation. Concrete file Read/Write/Seek member handoffs also use spans or the scoped origin.

verification.remaining: Record/element-count buffers, stream mode strings, file/path result interfaces, the explicitly retained text-writer count boundary and Milestone D remain active.

record_streams.contract: The functions still throw the existing StarsError on a short/failed nonempty file operation. Empty ranges perform no IO, including no Windows zero-write truncation, and do not advance the memory cursor. Memory-backed reads copy the exact requested bytes and advance by the same amount. Partial header/data publication and alert ordering are unchanged.
record_streams.capacities: Local/state arrays carry their actual extent and logical prefix. Universe-definition input uses its exact cb+1 allocation after the existing size check. Batch input uses the same uint16_t request as its arena allocation. Tutorial writes use the SizeofResource extent plus record offset/length. Report literals and fields retain exact lengths without NUL; two mutable/void literal casts are removed.
record_streams.wire_contract: The two-byte header, fixed record widths, XOR/seed order, and physical 1024-byte payload whose ten-bit header wraps are unchanged. No new record-length rejection or baseline movement is intended.
record_streams.characterization: Before migration the actual memory/file helpers passed sentinel-protected binary copies, cursor advancement, empty memory ranges and empty writes preserving file size/position. Those assertions are migrated to the span signatures alongside the existing short-read, partial-header callback and 1024-byte framing cases.
record_streams.remaining: WriteRt and its actual RECORDIO providers still use a separate payload pointer/length. CReadNative/CWriteNative element interfaces, memory-source cursor bounds and batch-file sizing/path parsing remain to migrate or audit. No source-bound guarantee is inferred from only bounding the destination.
